fields.name: userRateLimitRequestsPerMinute
fields.doc: Per-user rate limit for standard users (Tenant Admins, Operators, Viewers). Requests per minute keyed by UPN. Default: 120.

fields.name: globalAdminRateLimitRequestsPerMinute

fields.name: planTierDefinitionsJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized plan tier definitions mapping tier name to rate limits and features. Example: {"free":{"apiRateLimit":60},"pro":{"apiRateLimit":300},"enterprise":{"apiRateLimit":1000}}

fields.name: platformStatsBlobSasUrl
fields.doc: Container SAS URL used by maintenance to publish platform stats JSON files. Expected format: https://{account}.blob.core.windows.net/{container}?sv=...&sig=...

fields.name: collectorIdleTimeoutMinutes
fields.doc: Idle timeout in minutes for periodic collectors (Performance, AgentSelfMetrics). When no real enrollment event (app install, ESP phase change, etc.) is detected within this window, collectors stop automatically to prevent session bloat. They restart automatically when new enrollment activity is detected. 0 = disabled (collectors run indefinitely). Default: 15 minutes.

fields.name: desktopDetectorNoCandidateTimeoutMinutes
fields.doc: DAD liveness threshold in minutes. When the V2 DesktopArrivalDetector polls for this duration without detecting either an excluded-user explorer.exe or a real user desktop, it emits a single desktop_detector_no_candidate observability event. State-change-only — NOT a periodic heartbeat; max 1 event per detector lifetime. Used to distinguish "user never logged in" from "detector wiring dead post-reboot" in sessions where desktop_arrived is missing. 0 = disabled (event never fires). Default: 10 minutes.

fields.name: excessiveEventCountThreshold
fields.doc: Maintenance alarm threshold: sessions with more events than this value trigger an ExcessiveSessionEvents ops alert (dispatched to Telegram/Teams). 0 = disabled. Default: 2000 (largest real sessions observed are ~500).

fields.name: excessiveEventAutoActionMode
fields.doc: Auto-action mode for runaway sessions whose EventCount exceeds ExcessiveEventAutoActionThreshold. One of "Off", "Block", or "Kill". Off (default) keeps the warn-only behaviour; Block stops the device's uploads for ExcessiveEventAutoActionDurationHours; Kill issues a remote self-destruct signal. Action runs in the 2h maintenance batch, is idempotent per session via ExcessiveEventsAutoActioned, and never downgrades an existing Kill to Block.

fields.name: excessiveEventAutoActionThreshold
fields.doc: Event-count threshold for auto-block/kill. Must be greater than ExcessiveEventCountThreshold so operators see the warn first. 0 disables regardless of ExcessiveEventAutoActionMode. Default: 2500.

fields.name: excessiveEventAutoActionDurationHours
fields.doc: Duration in hours for the device block created by the auto-action path. Default: 24.

fields.name: opsEventRetentionDays
fields.doc: Retention period in days for operational events in the OpsEvents table. Events older than this are deleted by the periodic maintenance job. 0 = no cleanup (not recommended). Default: 90 days.

fields.name: slaNotificationCooldownHours
fields.doc: Cooldown in hours between repeat SLA breach notifications for the same tenant + breach type. Persisted via SlaTenantStatus so it survives Function host recycles. Default: 24 hours (one notification per day). Range: 1-168.

fields.name: feedbackEnabled
fields.doc: Global kill-switch for the in-app feedback prompt. When false, no user sees the feedback bubble regardless of other settings. Default: true.

fields.name: feedbackMinTenantAgeDays
fields.doc: Minimum tenant age in days before users are prompted for feedback. Prevents asking brand-new tenants who haven't had meaningful experience yet. Default: 14 days.

fields.name: feedbackCooldownDays
fields.doc: Cooldown in days after a user interacts with the feedback prompt before they are prompted again. 0 = never re-prompt (single wave only). Default: 60 days.

fields.name: diagnosticsGlobalLogPathsJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized list of global diagnostics log paths/wildcards to include in the diagnostics ZIP package for all tenants. Each entry: { "path": "...", "description": "...", "isBuiltIn": true }

fields.name: maxDiagnosticsDownloadSizeMB
fields.doc: Maximum allowed diagnostics download size in MB. Blobs exceeding this are rejected before streaming (413). 0 = no limit. Default: 500 MB.

fields.name: diagnosticsDownloadTimeoutSeconds
fields.doc: Timeout in seconds for the entire diagnostics download+stream operation. 0 = no timeout. Default: 120 seconds.

fields.name: mcpAccessPolicy
fields.doc: Controls who can access the remote MCP server. "Disabled" = MCP off, "WhitelistOnly" = GlobalAdmins + McpUsers table (default), "AllMembers" = any authenticated user.

fields.name: nvdApiKey
fields.doc: NVD API key for higher rate limits (50 req/30s vs 5 req/30s without key). Free registration at https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/request-an-api-key null = operate without API key (slower, still functional).

fields.name: opsAlertRulesJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized list of OpsAlertRule objects defining which event types trigger notifications. Provider-agnostic — rules apply to all enabled providers.

fields.name: opsAlertTelegramEnabled
fields.doc: Whether the Telegram alert provider is enabled. Default: false.

fields.name: opsAlertTelegramChatId
fields.doc: Telegram chat ID for ops alerts (e.g. ITEngineer channel).

fields.name: opsAlertTeamsEnabled
fields.doc: Whether the Teams alert provider is enabled. Default: false.

fields.name: opsAlertTeamsWebhookUrl
fields.doc: Teams Workflow webhook URL for ops alerts.

fields.name: opsAlertSlackEnabled
fields.doc: Whether the Slack alert provider is enabled. Default: false.

fields.name: opsAlertSlackWebhookUrl
fields.doc: Slack Incoming Webhook URL for ops alerts.

fields.name: opsNotificationChannelsJson
fields.doc: JSON array of platform notification channels (NotificationChannel), the destinations an OpsAlertRule can target by id. Supersedes the three fixed provider slots above: each channel carries its own provider, destination and name, so an operator can keep e.g. an "IT Engineer" push channel and a "Sales" webhook apart and bind each event type to only the channels that should see it. Null/empty = not migrated yet — then synthesizes the list from the legacy slots, so dispatch behavior is unchanged until an operator saves the section once.

fields.name: latestAgentV2Version
fields.doc: Version string of the latest published V2 agent (e.g. "2.0.647").

fields.name: latestAgentV2Sha256
fields.doc: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the latest published V2 agent ZIP.

fields.name: latestAgentV2ExeSha256
fields.doc: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the latest published V2 agent EXE.

fields.name: latestBootstrapV2ScriptVersion
fields.doc: Version string of the latest published V2 bootstrap script.

fields.name: allowAgentDowngrade
fields.doc: When true, the agent's self-updater is allowed to install a version strictly lower than the one it is currently running. Default: false (forward-only updates; prevents dev builds from being silently downgraded via the runtime_hash_mismatch force path). Set to true only for controlled rollback scenarios — flip back to false immediately afterwards. Single global flag; applies to whichever line the calling agent runs on.

fields.name: agentMigrateApiBaseUrl
fields.doc: Global migration target served to ALL agents as AgentConfigResponse.MigrateToApiBaseUrl (e.g. "https://autopilotmonitor-api-us.azurewebsites.net"). Empty = no global migration. Set this on the backend being ABANDONED; clear it once the migration window closes. Per-tenant overrides in AgentMigrateTenantOverridesJson win over this.

fields.name: agentMigrateTenantOverridesJson
fields.doc: JSON object mapping tenantId → migration target URL for per-tenant moves (e.g. one tenant relocating EU→US). An entry with an EMPTY string value pins that tenant to the current backend even while AgentMigrateApiBaseUrl is set (staged rollout). Example: {"11111111-...": "https://autopilotmonitor-api-us.azurewebsites.net", "22222222-...": ""}

fields.name: modernDeploymentHarmlessEventIdsJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized list of Windows ModernDeployment EventIDs that are considered harmless. Matching events (Level 2 Error or Level 3 Warning) are downgraded to Debug severity by the agent — they stay visible for troubleshooting but do not surface as Error/Warning in the session timeline and are ignored by the stall-probe anomaly scan. Level 1 Critical is never downgraded. Example: "[100, 1005, 1010]"

fields.name: whiteGloveSealingPatternIdsJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized list of ImeLogPattern IDs whose match is re-emitted by the V2 agent as a WhiteGloveSealingPatternDetected DecisionSignal (in addition to the normal ime_pattern_match event). Example: "[\"wg-seal-1\",\"wg-seal-2\"]". Default null/empty = feature off (M3-compatible, no regression risk). Only IDs in this list count as sealing signals; other IME pattern matches follow the regular event path. Global-only — no per-tenant override (plan §M5 M4.4.5.e decision).

fields.name: vulnerabilityCorrelationEnabled
fields.doc: Whether vulnerability correlation is globally enabled. When false, agents still collect inventory but backend skips correlation. Default: true

fields.name: enableIndexDualWrite
fields.doc: Feature flag for V2 Decision Engine index-table dual-write (Plan §M5.d). When true, IngestTelemetryFunction enqueues telemetry-index-reconcile envelopes after committing each primary Signals / DecisionTransitions row; a queue-triggered handler (M5.d.3) then writes the 0–3 applicable index rows. Default: false — enables controlled rollout. The 2h reconcile timer (M5.d.4) is the safety-net for queue failures even once the flag is on.

fields.name: autoApproveNewTenants
fields.doc: When true, new tenant signups are activated automatically ~1 minute after first sign-in (tenant-auto-approve queue worker). When false, every signup waits for a manual Global Admin approval in Tenant Management. Default false — the operator opts into auto-activation and can flip it off at any time (e.g. on abuse) to return to manual vetting; messages already in the queue are then dropped, not parked. Round-tripped via the 4-file web chain (memory feedback_admin_config_ui_roundtrip).

fields.name: imeMsiArchivingEnabled
fields.doc: When true, the first fleet-wide sighting of a new IME version enqueues an archive job (ime-msi-archive queue) that downloads the installer from the CSP-reported URL into the ime-archive blob container. Roughly one download per Microsoft IME release (~monthly). Default true — flip off to pause archiving (queued messages then wait, they are not dropped). Round-tripped via the 4-file web chain (memory feedback_admin_config_ui_roundtrip).

fields.name: maxImeMsiDownloadSizeMB
fields.doc: Size cap for the IME installer download in MB (Content-Length preflight AND streamed-byte guard). The MSI is ~12 MB today; the generous cap exists only so a tampered/wrong URL cannot stream gigabytes into the archive while still never missing a legitimately grown installer. 0 = no limit. Default: 250 MB.

fields.name: selfServiceAppHomingEnabled
fields.doc: When true, the dual app-registration self-service homing flip is active: the Graph consent flow funnels legacy-homed tenants to the primary (new) app registration and auto-flips TenantConfiguration.HomedAppClientId once admin consent for the primary app is verified; tenant admins may also flip manually via POST config/{tenantId}/app-homing. When false (kill switch) all of the above stops immediately — consent URLs mint for the homed app again and only Global Admins can flip. Default false — the operator enables it after the dual-app config swap. Round-tripped via the 4-file web chain (memory feedback_admin_config_ui_roundtrip).

fields.name: sessionDeletionKillSwitch
fields.doc: Global emergency kill-switch for the cascade-deletion subsystem (Plan §1 P8 / §9). When true: cascade producers return 503 Service Unavailable;the cascade worker returns its message to the queue on entry without processing. Round-tripped via the 4-file web chain (memory feedback_admin_config_ui_roundtrip) so admin saves preserve it. Default false.

fields.name: vulnerabilityDataLastSyncUtc
fields.doc: Last successful CISA KEV catalog sync timestamp (UTC ISO 8601). Updated by VulnerabilityDataSyncFunction (daily timer) and TriggerVulnerabilityDataSyncFunction (manual /api/vulnerability/sync). Pre-existing field — semantically means "last KEV sync" since KEV is the only live data refresh that ran via the manual endpoint historically.

fields.name: msrcLastSyncUtc
fields.doc: Last successful MSRC CVRF index refresh timestamp (UTC ISO 8601). Updated by VulnerabilityDataSyncFunction (daily timer) and TriggerMsrcSyncFunction (manual /api/vulnerability/sync-msrc). Empty/null means MSRC has never refreshed successfully since this field was introduced.

fields.name: nvdCacheLastRefreshUtc
fields.doc: Last COMPLETED refresh of the stale NVD CVE cache rows (UTC ISO 8601) — a run that walked every stale row without being cut short by an NVD throttle cooldown. Updated by VulnerabilityDataSyncFunction (daily timer) and the manual /api/vulnerability/sync-nvd.

fields.name: epssLastSyncUtc
fields.doc: Last successful FIRST EPSS re-score of the cached CVEs (UTC ISO 8601). Updated by VulnerabilityDataSyncFunction (daily timer) and the manual /api/vulnerability/sync-epss.

AdminIdentityBinding.doc: The immutable Entra identity behind a cross-tenant-role UPN: the HOME tenant the UPN was granted for and, once known, the user's object id. fields.name: objectId

fields.name: objectIdPinnedAt

fields.name: agentVersion

AnalyzeRule.doc: Defines how to analyze collected events to detect issues Analyze rules run server-side during event ingestion

fields.name: ruleId
fields.doc: Unique rule identifier (e.g., "ANALYZE-NET-001")

fields.name: title
fields.doc: Human-readable rule title (e.g., "Proxy Authentication Required")

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Detailed description of what this rule detects

fields.name: severity
fields.doc: Severity level: "info", "warning", "high", "critical"

fields.name: category
fields.doc: Rule category: network, identity, enrollment, apps, esp, device

fields.name: version
fields.doc: Semantic version of this rule (e.g., "1.0.0")

fields.name: author
fields.doc: Author of this rule

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether this rule is currently enabled for the tenant

fields.name: isBuiltIn
fields.doc: Whether this is a built-in rule (shipped with the system)

fields.name: isCommunity
fields.doc: Whether this is a community-contributed rule Community rules behave like built-in rules (read-only, state stored separately) but are displayed with a distinct "Community" badge in the portal

fields.name: provenance
fields.doc: Where this global rule row came from — see RuleProvenance. Drives the self-maintaining sunset: "embedded"/null = owned by the deployed binary's catalog (may be sunset when it leaves that catalog); "github" = reseeded from GitHub ahead of the binary (exempt from the embedded catalog sunset/filter). Null on pre-existing rows = embedded.

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: Rule trigger type: "single" (matches individual events) or "correlation" (combines multiple event types) Both types run at the same time during analysis - this field is organizational/descriptive

fields.name: evaluateOn
fields.doc: When this rule is evaluated. Null/empty = ["enrollment_end"] — the historical terminal-only behavior. Additional interim triggers let a rule fire before the session is terminal: "whiteglove_sealed" (first genuine whiteglove_complete seal) and "on_event:<eventType>" (an ingest batch contained that event type). Interim runs suppress the KO path and record no stats — see AnalyzeRuleTriggers and internal/docs/rules/analyze-rule-triggers.md.

fields.name: preconditions
fields.doc: Optional device-fact gates evaluated BEFORE conditions. ALL preconditions must pass; if any fails the rule is silently skipped — no result, no UI card. Used to filter out hardware/OS profiles where a rule does not apply (e.g. "skip on virtual machines").

fields.name: conditions
fields.doc: Conditions that must be evaluated against the event stream All required conditions must match for the rule to fire

fields.name: baseConfidence
fields.doc: Base confidence score (0-100) when the rule's required conditions match Additional confidence is added from ConfidenceFactors

fields.name: confidenceFactors
fields.doc: Additional factors that increase confidence when matched

fields.name: confidenceThreshold
fields.doc: Minimum confidence score (0-100) to create a RuleResult Default: 40

fields.name: explanation
fields.doc: Detailed explanation of the detected issue Supports markdown formatting

fields.name: remediation
fields.doc: Steps to remediate the detected issue

fields.name: relatedDocs
fields.doc: Links to relevant documentation

fields.name: templateVariables
fields.doc: Template variables that must be customized per-tenant before the rule can be used. If non-empty, the rule is a template: enabling it creates a tenant custom copy with the user's values substituted into the conditions.

fields.name: derivedFromTemplateRuleId
fields.doc: If this custom rule was created from a template, stores the original template rule's ID. Used to track lineage and prevent duplicate copies.

fields.name: markSessionAsFailedDefault
fields.doc: Rule-definition default for whether firing this rule should mark the entire session as failed. Shipped in the rule JSON. A tenant can override this via MarkSessionAsFailed in their RuleState — a firing rule is considered a "KO criterion" for the enrollment when the effective value (override ?? default) is true.

fields.name: markSessionAsFailed
fields.doc: Tenant-scoped override for MarkSessionAsFailedDefault. Not persisted in the rule JSON — populated at load time from the RuleStates table. Null means the tenant has not expressed a preference (fall back to the default).

fields.name: notifyDefault
fields.doc: Rule-definition default for whether newly detected findings of this rule send an outbound notification. Off for all shipped rules — notification targets are tenant-specific channel ids, so notify only becomes actionable through the tenant override + channel selection.

fields.name: notify
fields.doc: Tenant-scoped override for NotifyDefault. Not persisted in the rule JSON — populated at load time from the RuleStates table. Null = no preference (use the default).

fields.name: notifyChannelIds
fields.doc: Tenant-scoped notification targets: ids of the tenant's notification channels (TenantConfiguration.NotificationChannelsJson) that receive an alert when this rule fires. Populated at load time from the RuleStates table alongside Notify. Effective notify requires both the flag and at least one resolvable channel id.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Tags for filtering and categorization

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: When this rule was created

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.doc: When this rule was last updated

fields.name: exitCode

fields.name: bucket
fields.doc: "day" (windows up to 30 days) or "week".

fields.name: detectionLiesCount
fields.doc: Succeeded installs whose detection re-check reported NotDetected.

fields.name: versionRegressions

AppAnalyticsSummary.doc: Headline aggregate of one app's analytics window.

fields.name: trend
fields.doc: "improving" | "worsening" | "stable".

fields.name: trendDelta
fields.doc: Absent when either window half has under 5 finished installs.

fields.name: flakinessScore
fields.doc: Share of installs with AttemptNumber > 1 (0-1, three decimals).

AppAnalyticsTimeBucket.doc: One day/week bucket of the analytics time series.

AppDeviceModelBreakdownItem.doc: Per device-model failure aggregate (lift vs the app's baseline rate, descending).

AppFailureCodeCount.doc: One failure code with its occurrence count.

AppHomingProbeWire.doc: Consent-probe verdict embedded in app-homing responses (success and deny alike). Built by AppHomingFunction.ProbePayload.

fields.name: attempted
fields.doc: False when the decision needed no probe (e.g. GA force flip).

fields.name: missingRoles
fields.doc: Legacy add-on Graph roles the primary app lacks (probe refused, not transient), or null — the key is omitted when null. The admin grants exactly these on the primary app.

fields.name: topFailingApps
fields.doc: Top failing apps by failure count.

AppMetricsAppGroup.doc: One app's aggregate across its install rows in the window.

fields.name: failureRate
fields.doc: Failed / (failed + succeeded) as a percentage; skips never count as attempts.

fields.name: avgDurationSeconds
fields.doc: Average measured FINAL-attempt duration (whole seconds); 0 with no measured installs.

fields.name: topFailureCodes
fields.doc: Top 3 failure codes by count, descending.

AppMetricsDeliveryOptimization.doc: Fleet-wide Delivery Optimization rollup across every install row in the window.

fields.name: peerOffloadPercent
fields.doc: Share of bytes not pulled from the CDN (peers + Microsoft Connected Cache), 0-100 one decimal.

AppMetricsResponse.doc: Response of GET metrics/app and GET global/metrics/app: per-app install health over the requested window (slowest apps by average FINAL-attempt duration, top failing apps) plus the fleet Delivery Optimization rollup.

fields.name: totalCollisionExcluded
fields.doc: Rows excluded from per-app groups because their name-keyed row merged distinct appIds.

AppSessionItem.doc: One install row of the app-sessions drilldown (failed first, then in-progress, newest first).

fields.name: exitCode
fields.doc: Absent when the install carried no exit code.

fields.name: installPassCount
fields.doc: 2+ = the IME processed this app in multiple passes (device-ESP evaluation + real install).

AppSessionsResponse.doc: Response of GET apps/{appName}/sessions and its global variant (offset-paged).

AppVersionRegressionAlert.doc: One ACTIVE app-version duration regression: an app whose newest version's median install duration rose ≥2× (and ≥5 minutes absolute) over the previous version's median, both sides with enough measured installs. Persisted as the appversionregression|{app}|{version} keyspace of the notification tracker table — the row IS the dedup (one bell per episode), and the versionRegressions[] payload on the app-analytics response. Deleted when the episode re-arms (median falls back under 1.5× or the version drains out of the horizon) or by the tracker's 30-day retention sweep. Numbers refresh on every radar pass while the episode stays active; FirstNotifiedAt never moves.

fields.name: currentVersion
fields.doc: The regressed (newer) version — episode key together with the app.

fields.name: previousVersion
fields.doc: The comparison version: latest first-seen strictly before the current version's first-seen.

fields.name: currentMeasuredCount
fields.doc: Measured installs backing each median (gate: both ≥10).

fields.name: lift
fields.doc: Current median ÷ previous median (gate: ≥2.0; previous median is never 0 — measured durations are ≥1s).

fields.name: firstNotifiedAt
fields.doc: When the episode first fired (bell + ops event moment). Never moves on refresh; drives the 30d retention re-arm.

fields.name: lastEvaluatedAt
fields.doc: Last radar pass that re-confirmed/refreshed this episode.

AppsListItem.doc: One app row of the apps list (failed desc, then failure rate, then name).

fields.name: trend
fields.doc: "improving" | "worsening" | "stable".

fields.name: trendDelta
fields.doc: Failure-rate delta between window halves; absent when either half has under 5 finished installs.

AppsListResponse.doc: Response of GET apps/list and GET global/apps/list. Legacy mode (no pageSize) returns the full array with the paging keys absent; opt-in pagination adds count/offset/pageSize and a nextLink while more pages remain.

fields.name: collisionExcluded
fields.doc: Rows excluded because their name-keyed row merged distinct appIds.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: Rows on this page; absent in legacy full-array mode.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: Absent in legacy full-array mode.

fields.name: pageSize
fields.doc: Absent in legacy full-array mode.

fields.name: nextLink
fields.doc: Next-page link; absent in legacy mode and on the last page.

AuditLogListResponse.doc: Shared response of the audit-log listing endpoints (GET audit/logs and GET global/audit/logs), paged and non-paged: the non-paged variant leaves NextLink null so the key is absent, exactly like the old literal.

fields.name: nextLink
fields.doc: Absolute-path link to the next page, or null on the last page / non-paged variant — the key is omitted when null.

AuthMeResponse.doc: Success body of GET auth/me: the caller's resolved identity, roles and effective entitlement flags. Blocked outcomes (TenantSuspended / PendingActivation) are error shapes and stay anonymous by design.

fields.name: isDelegated

fields.name: delegatedTenantIds
fields.doc: The OTHER tenants this caller may manage; empty for non-delegated callers.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: Tenant role (Admin / Operator / Viewer); the key is omitted for a roleless caller.

fields.name: homedApp
fields.doc: "primary" or "legacy" — which app registration this tenant is homed on.

fields.doc: empty_name | empty_keyword | nvd_throttled | nvd_unavailable | no_match | no_results | nvd_api_error.

fields.name: appHomingPending
fields.doc: True when the homing auto-flip was deferred (consent still propagating / transient) — a retry converges.

fields.name: appHomingMissingRoles
fields.doc: Legacy add-on Graph roles the primary app lacks, blocking the homing flip until granted on the primary app; null when nothing blocks — the key is omitted when null.

fields.name: willAutoFlipHoming

BackfillResult.doc: Run report of the one-shot OccurredUtc backfill (POST maintenance/backfill-occurred-utc).

DeviceHistory.doc: Per-device enrollment history for F2 (insights spec §F2) — one row per device key (TenantId, normalized serial), holding the compact chain of the device's terminal sessions (capped at the 20 most recent) plus derived journey counts. Written inline at every session-terminal transition (so the session-detail banner is fresh) and healed by the rolling maintenance sweep, which also drops refs of deleted sessions (tombstone-driven) and deletes the row when the chain empties. Junk serials (placeholder identities) never get a row. Persisted in DeviceHistories; wiped on tenant offboarding — deliberately NOT part of the per-session deletion manifest, because the row aggregates many sessions.

fields.name: serialKey
fields.doc: Normalized device key component: trimmed + lower-cased serial (spec: trim + case-fold).

fields.name: serialNumber
fields.doc: Display serial as last reported (trimmed, original casing).

fields.name: chain
fields.doc: Terminal session refs ordered by StartedAt ascending, capped at the 20 most recent.

fields.name: currentJourneyAttempts
fields.doc: Attempt count of the LAST journey in the chain (open or completed) — the "Attempt N" the session banner shows.

fields.name: journeyCount
fields.doc: Journeys represented in the retained chain (the 20-cap can hide older journeys — this is a chain-scoped count, not a lifetime claim).

fields.name: journeyVersion
fields.doc: Journey-grouping algorithm version (truthfulness rule 8: a definition change never silently mixes semantics).

DeviceJourneyAttemptBucket.doc: One attempt-histogram bucket: how many completed journeys took exactly Attempts attempts.

DeviceJourneyDailyAggregate.doc: Daily First-Time-Right rollup for one (tenant, date) — F2 PR4 (insights spec §F2). A journey counts on the StartedAt date of its COMPLETING success session (same StartedAt-date bucketing as every other daily aggregate; the rolling sweep re-buckets late-terminating sessions idempotently). Only journeys that ended with a terminal success are counted — open journeys (no success yet, incl. WhiteGlove waiting for its user session) and gap-abandoned journeys never enter numerator or denominator. Counts are additive across days, so a window rate is the sum of daily rows — no rolling-window row is needed (unlike the median-based time-attribution aggregates). Rows are written even below the ≥20-completed-journeys UI gate: the UI needs the n to say "insufficient data (n=3)" (truthfulness rule 4). Junk-serial exclusions are disclosed per day (rule 7). "global" mirror rows sum all tenants.

fields.name: date
fields.doc: Calendar day (UTC, "yyyy-MM-dd") the completing success sessions STARTED.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Tenant GUID, or "global" for the cross-tenant row.

fields.name: journeyVersion
fields.doc: Journey-grouping algorithm version the counts were computed with (rule 8).

fields.name: completedJourneyCount
fields.doc: Journeys completed (first terminal success) on this date — the FTR denominator.

fields.name: firstTimeRightCount
fields.doc: Completed journeys with attempt count == 1 — the FTR numerator.

fields.name: attemptHistogram
fields.doc: Attempt distribution across the completed journeys, ordered by attempts ascending.

fields.name: excludedSessionCount
fields.doc: Terminal sessions on this date excluded for junk/placeholder serials — disclosed, never silent (rule 7).

DeviceJourneyMetricsResponse.doc: Response of GET metrics/device-journeys and GET global/metrics/device-journeys: daily First-Time-Right rows of the window plus their sums, the merged attempt histogram, and the repeat-devices violator list (absent on the cross-tenant aggregate).

fields.name: daily
fields.doc: Daily rows of the window, date ordinal order.

fields.name: repeatDevices
fields.doc: Devices whose current journey took at least 2 attempts; absent on the cross-tenant aggregate (no per-device drill there).

DeviceJourneyRepeatDevice.doc: One repeat-device violator row (current journey took at least 2 attempts, newest terminal session in the window).

fields.name: lastFailureReason

DeviceJourneyWindowTotals.doc: Window totals of the device-journey response (additive sums over the daily rows).

fields.name: ftrRatePct

DeviceNotRegisteredItem.doc: One serial-number bucket in the GetDeviceNotRegistered aggregation. All values are self-reported by devices through the unauthenticated distress channel — UNVERIFIED.

DeviceSessionRef.doc: One terminal session of a device inside its Chain — the compact ref the F2 journey grouping runs on (insights spec §F2). fields.name: completedAt
fields.doc: Terminal timestamp; feeds the 30-day journey-gap rule (fallback: StartedAt).

fields.name: status
fields.doc: SessionStatus name ("Succeeded" / "Failed" / "Incomplete").

fields.name: enrollmentType

EnrollmentEvent.doc: Represents a single event during enrollment

fields.name: eventId
fields.doc: Unique identifier for this event

fields.name: sessionId
fields.doc: Session identifier this event belongs to

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Tenant identifier

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: Timestamp when the agent detected/created this event on the device (UTC). Set at construction time (DateTime.UtcNow) or from the source's native timestamp (e.g., Windows EventLog TimeCreated). The backend stores this as-is — it is the authoritative "agent-side" timestamp, not a server-side receive time.

fields.name: receivedAt
fields.doc: Server-side UTC timestamp set when the backend receives and stores this event. Null for events that pre-date this feature. Never set by the agent.

fields.name: sentAt
fields.doc: Device-clock UTC timestamp of the moment the agent SENT the upload batch carrying this event (X-Send-Time-Utc request header, one value per ingest request — never set by the agent per event). Same clock frame as Timestamp, so SentAt − Timestamp is pure spool delay and ReceivedAt − SentAt is network latency plus device-vs-server clock offset — the two are indistinguishable without this field. Null for events from agents that pre-date the header.

fields.name: eventType
fields.doc: Type of event (e.g., "phase_transition", "app_install_start", "error")

fields.name: severity
fields.doc: Severity as string for JSON serialization

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Source of the event — typically the producing class name (e.g. "ImeLogTracker", "EnrollmentTracker", "DecisionEngine") or a stable lifecycle label ("Agent").

fields.name: phase
fields.doc: Phase as number for JSON serialization (frontend expects number)

fields.name: phaseName
fields.doc: Phase name as string for JSON serialization

fields.name: message
fields.doc: Human-readable message

fields.name: data
fields.doc: Additional structured data

fields.name: sequence
fields.doc: Sequence number for ordering events with same timestamp

fields.name: originalTimestamp
fields.doc: Original agent-side timestamp preserved when the backend clamps an out-of-range value. Null when the timestamp was within the valid range and no correction was needed. Use this for troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of clock issues on devices.

fields.name: timestampClamped
fields.doc: True when the backend had to clamp the agent-side Timestamp to a valid range. When set, OriginalTimestamp contains the raw value the agent sent. AI analysis and UI should treat clamped timestamps with caution.

fields.name: rowKey
fields.doc: Azure Table Storage RowKey — format: {Timestamp:yyyyMMddHHmmssfff}_{Sequence:D10} Represents the exact sort key used in storage.

fields.name: causedByTransitionStepIndex
fields.doc: Reducer StepIndex of the DecisionTransition whose EmitEventTimelineEntry effect produced this event. Nullable for forward-compat (events that pre-date Codex follow-up #3 or that are emitted outside the reducer pipeline). Together with CausedBySignalOrdinal this replaces the always-empty DecisionTransition.EmittedEventSequences — the forward link lives on the event side because the event's Sequence is assigned after the journal record is already on disk.

fields.name: causedBySignalOrdinal
fields.doc: SessionSignalOrdinal of the signal that drove the transition which emitted this event. Nullable for the same reason as CausedByTransitionStepIndex. Lets the Inspector jump "event → causing signal" without joining through the transitions table.

EpssRefreshRunWire.doc: Outcome of the last EPSS re-score run on THIS instance (in-memory).

fields.name: startedUtc
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 start timestamp.

fields.name: finishedUtc
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 finish timestamp, or null (key omitted) while still running.

FeedbackEligibilityResponse.doc: Response of GET feedback/eligibility: whether the caller should be shown the feedback prompt.

FeedbackEntryWire.doc: One feedback interaction as rendered on the Global Admin dashboard.

fields.name: rating
fields.doc: Absent on dismissals.

fields.name: comment
fields.doc: Absent on dismissals.

fields.doc: ISO-8601 round-trip string; absent when never stamped.

FeedbackListResponse.doc: Response of GET feedback/all (Global Admin dashboard): every stored feedback entry.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: All sessions on this model in the window, including in-flight ones.

fields.name: failureRate
fields.doc: Failed / (Failed + Succeeded) * 100, rounded — finished enrollments only.

FleetHealthMetrics.doc: Server-computed Fleet Health aggregates. Replaces the client-side pass that drained up to 200k raw sessions into the browser and aggregated on the main thread. Built once per request from the windowed session list — see MetricsMath.BuildFleetHealthPayload. Presentation-only derivations (bar-chart maxima, weekday/month axis labels) stay on the client; this payload carries the data, not the formatting.

fields.name: dailyData
fields.doc: One entry per day in the window, oldest-first. Date is UTC "yyyy-MM-dd".

fields.name: failureReasons
fields.doc: Top failure reasons by count (descending).

fields.name: modelHealth
fields.doc: Device models by enrollment volume (descending).

fields.name: slowestModels
fields.doc: Device models by average successful enrollment duration (descending).

fields.name: topFailingModels
fields.doc: Device models by failure count (descending).

fields.name: incomplete
fields.doc: Terminal, non-failure sessions (timeout reclassification). Surfaced as its own count; not a failure.

fields.name: successRate
fields.doc: Succeeded / (Succeeded + Failed) * 100 (one decimal) — finished enrollments only, matching the SLA convention. 0 when nothing has finished yet (clients render "—").

fields.name: avgDurationMinutes
fields.doc: Average duration in minutes over non-in-progress sessions that carry a duration. Kept for API compatibility; the cards lead with the median, which a handful of multi-hour outliers (overnight ESP, WhiteGlove late user phase) cannot drag around.

fields.name: medianDurationMinutes
fields.doc: Median duration in minutes over the same population as AvgDurationMinutes.

fields.name: p90DurationMinutes
fields.doc: 90th-percentile duration in minutes over the same population — the tail signal the median alone would hide.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: All sessions on this model in the window, including in-flight ones.

fields.name: failed
fields.doc: Clients derive the per-model rate as Succeeded / (Succeeded + Failed).

GatherRule.doc: Defines what data the agent should collect Gather rules are delivered to the agent via the config API and can be managed (enabled/disabled, created) through the portal

fields.name: ruleId
fields.doc: Unique rule identifier (e.g., "GATHER-NET-001")

fields.name: title
fields.doc: Human-readable rule title (e.g., "Collect WinHTTP Proxy Settings")

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Detailed description of what this rule collects and why

fields.name: category
fields.doc: Rule category: network, identity, apps, device, esp, enrollment

fields.name: version
fields.doc: Semantic version of this rule (e.g., "1.0.0")

fields.name: author
fields.doc: Author of this rule

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether this rule is currently enabled for the tenant

fields.name: isBuiltIn
fields.doc: Whether this is a built-in rule (shipped with the system) Built-in rules cannot be deleted, only disabled

fields.name: isCommunity
fields.doc: Whether this is a community-contributed rule Community rules behave like built-in rules (read-only, state stored separately) but are displayed with a distinct "Community" badge in the portal

fields.name: provenance
fields.doc: Where this global rule row came from — see RuleProvenance. Drives the self-maintaining sunset: "embedded"/null = owned by the deployed binary's catalog (may be sunset when it leaves that catalog); "github" = reseeded from GitHub ahead of the binary (exempt from the embedded catalog sunset/filter). Null on pre-existing rows = embedded.

fields.name: collectorType
fields.doc: Type of data collection: - "registry": Read values from the Windows Registry - "eventlog": Read entries from a Windows Event Log - "wmi": Execute a WMI/CIM query - "file": Check file/directory existence and optionally read content - "command_allowlisted": Run a pre-approved command (PowerShell or CLI). Only commands on the agent's hardcoded allowlist in GatherRuleExecutor.cs are permitted. Unlisted commands are blocked and generate a security_warning event. See the allowlist in GatherRuleExecutor.cs for the full list of approved commands. - "logparser": Parse a CMTrace-format log file using a regex pattern with named capture groups

fields.name: target
fields.doc: Target for collection: - registry: Registry path (e.g., "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\...") - eventlog: Event log name (e.g., "Microsoft-Windows-DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider/Admin") - wmi: WMI query (e.g., "SELECT * FROM Win32_TPM WHERE __NAMESPACE='root\\CIMV2\\Security\\MicrosoftTpm'") - file: File or directory path with env vars (e.g., "C:\Windows\INF\setupapi.dev.log") - command_allowlisted: Exact command string as it appears in the allowlist (e.g., "Get-Tpm", "dsregcmd /status") - logparser: Log file path with env vars (e.g., "%ProgramData%\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs\AppWorkload.log")

fields.name: parameters
fields.doc: Additional parameters for the collector: - registry: { "valueName": "ProxyServer" } — omit to read all values - eventlog: { "maxEntries": "10", "source": "...", "eventId": "62407", "messageFilter": "*ESPProgress*" } - wmi: { "namespace": "root\\CIMV2\\Security\\MicrosoftTpm" } - file: { "readContent": "true" } — only reads files <50 KB - command_allowlisted: (no additional parameters — command is the full string in Target) - logparser: { "pattern": "regex with (?<namedGroups>)", "trackPosition": "true", "maxLines": "1000" }

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: Trigger type: "startup", "phase_change", "phase_exit", "interval", "on_event". "phase_change" fires once when the phase in is ENTERED, "phase_exit" once when it is LEFT — the two one-shot bookends of a phase.

fields.name: intervalSeconds
fields.doc: Interval in seconds (only used when Trigger = "interval")

fields.name: triggerPhase
fields.doc: Phase to trigger on (used when Trigger = "phase_change" or "phase_exit"). Canonical tokens are the EnrollmentPhase enum names, e.g. "DeviceSetup", "AccountSetup", "Complete". Empty = every phase transition.

fields.name: triggerEventType
fields.doc: Event type to trigger on (only used when Trigger = "on_event") e.g., "app_install_failed"

fields.name: activePhases
fields.doc: Restricts the rule to run only while the current enrollment phase is one of these phases. Canonical tokens are the EnrollmentPhase enum names ("Start", "DevicePreparation", "DeviceSetup", "AppsDevice", "AccountSetup", "AppsUser", "FinalizingSetup", "Complete"); "Unknown" and "Failed" are rejected by backend validation. Null or empty = unrestricted (runs in every phase — legacy behavior). Mutually exclusive with ActiveFromPhase; if both are set the agent defensively prefers this list. Applies to ALL trigger types. Before the first phase signal of a session, scoped rules are inactive.

fields.name: activeFromPhase
fields.doc: Activates the rule once the enrollment phase first reaches this phase (ordinal comparison on EnrollmentPhase, ignoring Unknown/Failed), then keeps it active for the rest of the session (sticky latch — including through Failed). Canonical tokens as in ActivePhases. Null = unrestricted. Mutually exclusive with ActivePhases.

fields.name: emitMode
fields.doc: Emit behavior for collected results: null / "always" = emit on every collection (legacy behavior); "on_change" = poll on the trigger cadence but emit only when the collected result differs from the last emitted one. The first in-scope result always emits; the suppressed poll count is carried on the next emitted event (suppressedPolls / suppressedSinceUtc in the event data).

fields.name: outputEventType
fields.doc: EventType for the emitted event (e.g., "gather_proxy_settings")

fields.name: outputSeverity
fields.doc: Severity for the emitted event Default: "Info"

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Tags for filtering and categorization

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: When this rule was created

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.doc: When this rule was last updated

GetCpeMappingsResponse.doc: Response of GET vulnerability/cpe-mappings: every mapping plus the count.

fields.name: history
fields.doc: Absent when the device has no history row — the banner simply stays hidden.

fields.name: attemptNumber
fields.doc: The requesting session's attempt number within its journey; absent without a ?sessionId= parameter, when the session is unknown, or when the position cannot be computed (fail-soft, never a guessed position).

GetGlobalAdminsResponse.doc: Response of GET auth/global-admins: every Global Admin/Reader row.

GetGlobalMcpUsageDailyResponse.doc: Global daily MCP/API usage summaries envelope (GetGlobalMcpUsageDaily). The MCP server paginates over the summaries key — its name is wire-critical.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Echo of the request filter; absent when the caller passed no tenantId.

GetGlobalMcpUsageResponse.doc: Global per-tenant MCP/API usage envelope (GetGlobalMcpUsage). The MCP server paginates over the records key — its name is wire-critical.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Echo of the request filter; absent when the caller passed no tenantId.

GetGraphPermissionsStatusResponse.doc: Response of GET tenants/{tenantId}/graph-permissions/status: the client id of the app homed for the tenant, the transient flag, the granted Graph app roles and the per-feature verdict matrix.

fields.name: clientId
fields.doc: ClientId of the app registration that acts for this tenant (empty string when unresolved, never null).

fields.name: isTransient
fields.doc: True when the snapshot is not authoritative (token-acquire timeout / transient failure) — the UI renders "try again".

GetIgnoredSoftwareResponse.doc: Response of GET vulnerability/ignored-software: the full ignore list.

GetLatestVersionsResponse.doc: Response of GET config/latest-versions: the latest published agent + bootstrap script versions (null slots when the version blob could not be fetched).

fields.name: source
fields.doc: "cache" or "blob".

GetMcpOrganizationUsageResponse.doc: Organization-wide MCP usage by user for the caller's OWN tenant (GetMcpOrganizationUsage): every account whose requests were charged to this tenant's organization budget — its own members and any delegated (MSP) administrators reading the tenant. Built from the tenant's organization counters.

fields.name: dateFrom
fields.doc: Effective range start (yyyyMMdd).

fields.name: dateTo
fields.doc: Effective range end (yyyyMMdd, inclusive).

GetMcpUserUsageResponse.doc: Per-user MCP/API usage envelope (GetMcpUserUsage). Non-global callers only receive the records attributed to their own tenant; a foreign oid and an unknown oid are indistinguishable (both 200 with empty records). The MCP server paginates over the records key — its name is wire-critical.

GetMcpUsersResponse.doc: Response of GET global/mcp-users: the effective MCP access policy name plus every whitelist row.

GetMyMcpUsageResponse.doc: Self-service MCP/API usage envelope (GetMyMcpUsage): the caller's own usage records plus resolved plan and quota state. The MCP server paginates over the records key — its name is wire-critical.

fields.doc: Absent when the token carries no UPN claim.

fields.name: usagePlan

fields.name: effectivePlan
fields.doc: Resolved effective plan (per-user override → tenant edition).

GetPlatformStatsResponse.doc: Landing-page platform stats envelope (GetPlatformStats, unauthenticated). When no stats row has been computed yet, the zero shape is served: all counters 0 with TotalSignedUpTenants and LastUpdated absent.

fields.name: totalSignedUpTenants
fields.doc: Absent on the not-yet-computed zero shape.

fields.name: lastUpdated
fields.doc: Always absent today: the computed shape never sets it, the zero shape sets null.

GetPreviewNotificationEmailResponse.doc: Response of GET preview/notification-email/{tenantId}. Empty string when no address is stored (never null — the site coalesces).

GetPreviewWhitelistResponse.doc: Response of GET preview/whitelist: every approved tenant (Global Admin only).

GetRuleHitSessionsResponse.doc: Session ids where a rule produced a result within the window (GetRuleHitSessions) — powers the dashboard's ?ruleId= deep link.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: True when the result hit the hit-set cap (2000) — the list is a lower bound.

fields.name: success
fields.doc: False when any rule result failed to persist during an on-demand reanalyze.

fields.name: results
fields.doc: All persisted results, including resolved findings (kept for audit).

fields.name: totalIssues
fields.doc: Count of open (unresolved) findings only.

fields.name: persistFailureRuleIds
fields.doc: Rule ids that failed to persist during the reanalyze — the key is omitted entirely when there were no failures (the happy-path contract stays unchanged).

GetScriptDisplayNamesResponse.doc: Response of POST tenants/{tenantId}/scripts/display-names: resolved Intune script display names keyed by the canonical ref string. Always 200, possibly partial — unresolved refs stay in the dictionary with a null VALUE (dictionary values are NOT subject to WhenWritingNull, so the key is emitted with an explicit JSON null).

fields.name: refs
fields.doc: Display name per canonical script ref ("Platform:{id}" / "Remediation:{id}"). IMPORTANT: dictionary KEYS do not run through the camelCase PropertyNamingPolicy (ApiJsonOptions sets no DictionaryKeyPolicy) — the ref strings are serialized verbatim, including the PascalCase type prefix. Pinned by GraphWireParityTests.

fields.name: malformed
fields.doc: Ref tokens from the request that failed to parse, or null when there were none — the key is omitted when null (the empty-body and empty-refs early-exit sites never wrote this key at all; they leave it null).

GetSessionAnnotationsResponse.doc: Response of GET sessions/{sessionId}/annotations: the annotation lanes visible to the caller plus the server-computed list of lanes the caller may write.

fields.name: writableLanes
fields.doc: Lanes the caller is allowed to write — the web renders lanes writable exactly when this list says so.

fields.name: mode

fields.name: inFlightHint

fields.name: sampleKeys

fields.name: estimatedSnapshotBytes

GetSessionDeletionManifestResponse.doc: Stored cascade-delete snapshot summary envelope (GetSessionDeletionManifest, mode=summary).

fields.name: mode
fields.doc: Always "summary" — full/download modes bypass the JSON envelope.

fields.name: source

fields.name: sampleKeys

fields.name: progress

GetSessionDeletionsListResponse.doc: Cross-tenant listing of sessions in a cascade-deletion state (GetSessionDeletionsList).

fields.name: strandedSinceMinutes
fields.doc: Echo of the request filter; absent unless the caller passed it.

GetSessionEventsResponse.doc: Session events envelope (GetSessionEvents, paginated and unpaginated paths). Events carries full EnrollmentEvent items, or dictionary projections of them when the caller passed a fields= subset.

fields.name: nextLink

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: True when signals or transitions hit a load cap or the payload budget.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: True when the result hit the row cap or the cumulative payload budget.

GetSessionTimeAttributionResponse.doc: Per-session time-attribution envelope (GetSessionTimeAttribution). A missing breakdown is a NORMAL outcome (pre-feature session, non-terminal, Incomplete — no wall clock).

fields.name: breakdown
fields.doc: Absent when no breakdown row exists — the UI simply omits the lane.

GetTenantConfigFieldsSchemaResponse.doc: Response of GET config/fields-schema: the machine-readable tenant-config field schema for the MCP write surface.

fields.name: sessionFilter
fields.doc: Echo of the optional sessionId filter; absent when not passed.

GetTenantsWithDeletionManifestsResponse.doc: Tenants that have at least one deletion-manifest blob (GetTenantsWithDeletionManifests).

GetUnmatchedSoftwareResponse.doc: Response of GET vulnerability/unmatched-software: one page of the aggregated report.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Total distinct unmatched titles before paging.

GetVulnerabilityReportResponse.doc: Response of GET sessions/{sessionId}/vulnerability-report on the rescan paths and the no-stored-report path. (A stored-report hit streams the raw report JSON directly and bypasses this DTO.)

fields.name: report
fields.doc: The freshly generated report, or null (key omitted) when there is none.

fields.name: rescanned
fields.doc: True on the ?rescan=true paths; null (key omitted) on the plain read.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: Human-readable outcome note on the no-inventory / no-findings rescan paths; null (key omitted) otherwise.

GetVulnerabilitySyncStatusResponse.doc: Response of GET vulnerability/sync-status: live KEV/MSRC/NVD/EPSS cache sizes, the persisted last-sync timestamps, and the in-memory last-run stats of this instance.

fields.name: kevLastSyncUtc
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 timestamp from AdminConfiguration, or null (key omitted) when never synced.

fields.name: nvdLastRun
fields.doc: Last run on THIS instance (in-memory; null / key omitted after a cold start).

fields.name: epssLastRun
fields.doc: Last run on THIS instance (in-memory; null / key omitted after a cold start).

GlobalAdminRow.doc: One Global Admin/Reader row on the wire. Deliberately NOT the storage entity: the ITableEntity keys (partitionKey/rowKey/eTag/timestamp) that the pre-2026-08-31 wire carried are storage internals and were dropped from the contract (no consumer read them).

fields.name: upn
fields.doc: User Principal Name (lowercase).

fields.name: role
fields.doc: "GlobalAdmin" or "GlobalReader" (legacy empty rows are normalized to GlobalAdmin).

GlobalAverages.doc: Global average benchmarks for geographic comparison.

fields.name: avgApiLatencyMs
fields.doc: Global request-weighted average agent→backend API latency (ms); 0 = no data yet

fields.name: medianApiLatencyMs
fields.doc: Global median of per-session average API latency (ms), robust against outliers; 0 = no data yet

fields.name: avgDoPercentPeerCaching
fields.doc: Global weighted average peer caching percentage

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromPeers
fields.doc: Total peer bytes across all locations with DO data

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromHttp
fields.doc: Total HTTP bytes across all locations with DO data

GlobalNotificationDto.doc: One in-app notification (global pool or tenant-scoped; both endpoints share this DTO). A null Href key is omitted (WhenWritingNull).

GraphFeatureStatusItem.doc: One feature row of the graph-permissions status matrix: the feature identifier, the granted verdict (null while the snapshot is transient) and the Graph application permissions the feature requires.

fields.name: granted
fields.doc: Granted verdict, or null when the snapshot is transient (verdict unknown) — the key is omitted when null.

HardwareRejectedItem.doc: One manufacturer+model bucket in the GetHardwareRejected aggregation. All values are self-reported by devices through the unauthenticated distress channel — UNVERIFIED.

fields.name: sampleSerialNumbers
fields.doc: Up to five distinct serial numbers from the bucket.

HardwareRejectedResponse.doc: Success body of GET audit/hardware-rejected: hardware-whitelist rejections aggregated by manufacturer+model over the distress-report retention window.

fields.name: totalRawReports
fields.doc: Count of raw HardwareNotAllowed distress reports before aggregation.

HealthCheck.doc: One health check result inside GET health/detailed / health/mcp. Details is a heterogeneous per-check bag by design (endpoint URLs only for Global Admins); a null Details key is omitted (WhenWritingNull).

HealthCheckResponse.doc: Response of GET health: liveness probe plus the backend build identity.

IdentityBindingListResponse.doc: Response of GET global/identity-bindings: every admin identity binding.

IdentityBindingResponse.doc: Response of PUT global/identity-bindings/{upn}: the created/replaced binding.

IgnoredSoftwareItem.doc: One entry of the persistent software ignore list.

fields.name: ignoredAt
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 timestamp; empty when the row carries none.

ImeLogPattern.doc: Defines a regex pattern for IME log parsing. Delivered from backend via agent config endpoint. Allows updating patterns without agent rebuild when Microsoft changes IME log formats.

fields.name: patternId
fields.doc: Unique pattern identifier (e.g., "IME-ESP-PHASE")

fields.name: category
fields.doc: Pattern category controlling when the pattern is active: - "always": Always active regardless of ESP phase - "currentPhase": Only active during the current ESP phase - "otherPhases": Only active during non-current ESP phases (for history/completed apps)

fields.name: pattern
fields.doc: Regex pattern string to match against IME log message content. Supports named capture groups (e.g., (?<id>...)) which are passed to the action handler. Uses {GUID} as placeholder for the standard GUID capture pattern.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: Action to perform when the pattern matches: - "setCurrentApp": Set the current app being processed (uses 'id' capture group) - "updateStateInstalled": Mark app as installed - "updateStateDownloading": Mark app as downloading (uses 'bytes'/'ofbytes' for progress) - "updateStateInstalling": Mark app as installing - "updateStateSkipped": Mark app as skipped/not applicable - "updateStateError": Mark app as errored - "updateStatePostponed": Mark app as postponed (e.g., timeout) - "espPhaseDetected": ESP phase transition detected (uses 'espPhase' capture group) - "imeStarted": IME agent started - "policiesDiscovered": App policies JSON discovered (uses 'policies' capture group) - "ignoreCompletedApp": Add current app to ignore list (already completed in prior phase) - "imeAgentVersion": IME version detected (uses 'agentVersion' capture group) - "espTrackStatus": ESP tracked install status update (uses 'from'/'to'/'id' capture groups) - "updateName": Update app name (uses 'id'/'name' capture groups) - "updateWin32AppState": Update from Win32 app state (uses 'id'/'state' capture groups) - "cancelStuckAndSetCurrent": Cancel stuck app and set new current (uses 'id' capture group)

fields.name: parameters
fields.doc: Optional extra parameters for the action handler. Examples: - { "phase": "AccountSetup" } for espPhaseDetected to force a specific phase - { "useCurrentApp": "true" } to use CurrentPackageId instead of captured 'id' - { "checkTo": "true" } to check the 'to' capture group value before applying state

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether this pattern is enabled. Allows disabling patterns without removing them.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Human-readable description of what this pattern detects and why. Not used by the agent — purely for documentation and UI display.

fields.name: isBuiltIn
fields.doc: Whether this is a built-in pattern (shipped with the system). Built-in patterns cannot be deleted, only disabled.

fields.name: baselineRate
fields.doc: Hit rate on the baseline version; null without a baseline.

fields.name: expected
fields.doc: True when the baseline rate is at or above the expected threshold.

fields.name: sessions
fields.doc: Sessions that delivered a histogram on this version (not the ImeVersionHistory session count).

fields.name: fleetSessions
fields.doc: Total sessions per ImeVersionHistory (includes sessions without a terminal run).

ImeVersionHistoryEntry.doc: A tracked IME version sighting. Permanent archive that survives data retention.

fields.name: corroboratedAt
fields.doc: UTC time of the first sighting from a tenant OTHER than FirstSeenTenantId; null while only the first-seen tenant has reported the version. A version is shown to ordinary tenant members only once it is corroborated this way or its installer was archived with a matching ProductVersion — a single tenant's devices (the least trusted principal) cannot publish a version to every other tenant on their own.

fields.name: msiArchiveStatus
fields.doc: Outcome of the automatic installer archiving (ImeMsiArchiver): Archived, Queued (re-queued by a later sighting) or a Failed:* status; null for versions sighted before the feature existed or while the first archive job is still queued. Like the FirstSeen* identifiers, the archive fields are only serialized for Global Admin callers.

fields.name: msiArchiveUpdatedAt
fields.doc: UTC time of the last archive-status change (queue/attempt); drives the re-queue backoff.

fields.name: msiArchiveBlobPath
fields.doc: Blob path inside the ime-archive container, e.g. 1.104.102.0/IntuneWindowsAgent.msi.

fields.name: msiSha256
fields.doc: SHA-256 of the archived installer (hex, lowercase).

fields.name: msiBytes
fields.doc: Size of the archived installer in bytes.

fields.name: msiSourceUrl
fields.doc: The URL the installer was downloaded from (CSP-reported or one of the distribution hosts).

ImeVersionHistoryLeanEntry.doc: Redacted IME version row served to non-global callers of GET metrics/ime-versions: the platform-wide rollout facts without the first-seen tenant/session identifiers or the archive columns (see GetImeVersionHistoryFunction.BuildResponsePayload).

IsGlobalAdminResponse.doc: Response of GET auth/is-global-admin: whether the caller holds the Global Admin platform role, echoing the caller's UPN.

fields.name: upn
fields.doc: Caller's UPN from the token, or null when the token carries no UPN claim — the key is omitted when null.

ListBackupsResponse.doc: Response of GET global/backups: every backupId in the critical-table-backups container, newest first. Serialized with SerializerOptions (the backup surface's own options), not the ApiJsonOptions pipeline.

ListRawTablesResponse.doc: Success body of GET /api/global/raw/tables (ListRawTables): the queryable table names.

ListTenantConfigBackupsResponse.doc: Response of GET config/{tenantId}/backups: the tenant's pre-write config snapshots, newest first.

LocationMetrics.doc: Performance metrics for a single geographic location.

fields.name: avgAppCount
fields.doc: Average number of apps installed per session at this location

fields.name: minutesPerApp
fields.doc: Average minutes per app (AvgDurationMinutes / AvgAppCount)

fields.name: appLoadScore
fields.doc: Normalized score: 100 = global median, lower is better

fields.name: avgThroughputBytesPerSec
fields.doc: Average download throughput in bytes/sec at this location

fields.name: durationVsGlobalPct
fields.doc: Percentage difference from global avg duration (negative = faster)

fields.name: throughputVsGlobalPct
fields.doc: Percentage difference from global avg throughput (positive = faster)

fields.name: avgApiLatencyMs
fields.doc: Average agent→backend HTTP round-trip (ms) at this location, weighted per session by its request count. 0 when no session here carries latency data (pre-feature agents). A single corrupt session average (e.g. a request spanning a sleep/hibernate) can dominate this figure — use MedianApiLatencyMs as the display statistic.

fields.name: medianApiLatencyMs
fields.doc: Median of the per-session average agent→backend round-trips (ms) at this location — robust against outlier sessions. 0 when no session here carries latency data.

fields.name: apiLatencySessionCount
fields.doc: Sessions at this location that carry API-latency data

fields.name: apiLatencyVsGlobalPct
fields.doc: Percentage difference from global median API latency (positive = slower/farther)

fields.name: outlierDirection
fields.doc: "fast", "slow", or null

fields.name: doSessionCount
fields.doc: Sessions at this location that have DO telemetry data

fields.name: avgDoPercentPeerCaching
fields.doc: Weighted percentage of bytes from peers (0-100), computed from total peer/total DO bytes

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromPeers
fields.doc: Total bytes downloaded from all peer sources

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromHttp
fields.doc: Total bytes downloaded from HTTP/CDN

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromLanPeers
fields.doc: Bytes from LAN peers

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromGroupPeers
fields.doc: Bytes from group peers

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromInternetPeers
fields.doc: Bytes from internet peers

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromLinkLocalPeers
fields.doc: Bytes from link-local peers (same subnet)

fields.name: totalDoBytesFromCacheServer
fields.doc: Bytes served from a Microsoft Connected Cache (MCC) — separate from BytesFromPeers

LocationSessionLeanRow.doc: Lean projection of LocationSessionRow used as the default drilldown row. Fields chosen to support the typical MCP triage flow (which session, when, where, how big a deal, was DO active). Built by GetGeographicLocationSessionsFunction.ToLeanRow.

fields.name: completedAt
fields.doc: Absent while the session has not completed.

fields.name: durationSeconds
fields.doc: Absent while the session carries no authoritative duration.

fields.name: doPercentPeerCaching
fields.doc: Weighted peer-caching percentage for this session (0-100, one decimal).

LocationSessionRow.doc: Session row returned by the geographic drilldown endpoint. Extends SessionSummary with per-session Delivery Optimization aggregates so the user can troubleshoot DO usage without leaving the drilldown view.

fields.name: hasDoTelemetry
fields.doc: True if any app in this session has DO telemetry (DoDownloadMode >= 0).

fields.name: doAppCount
fields.doc: Number of apps in this session that have DO telemetry.

fields.name: totalAppCount
fields.doc: Total number of app install summaries recorded for this session.

fields.name: doPercentPeerCaching
fields.doc: Weighted peer-caching percentage for this session (0-100).

LogPatternLineResult.doc: Per-line outcome row of one pattern test.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: matched | no_match | parse_failed | regex_timeout

fields.name: groups
fields.doc: The named/numbered capture groups exactly as they would land in the emitted event's data (group "0" excluded, unsuccessful groups omitted).

fields.name: component
fields.doc: cmtrace mode only: the parsed component/type/message the regex ran against.

LogPatternTestResult.doc: Aggregate outcome of one pattern test. Serialized camelCase to clients.

MaintenanceResult.doc: Run report of a manual maintenance run (POST maintenance/trigger).

ManagedTenantItem.doc: One managed tenant as the managing tenant sees it.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: self-service (joined by invitation, removable here) | operator (provisioned by platform operators).

fields.name: usage
fields.doc: Absent when not resolved (cap reached or read failure).

ManagedTenantQuotaUsage.doc: MCP organization budget of a managed tenant, nested in ManagedTenantItem.

McpHealthCheckResponse.doc: Response of GET health/mcp: the standalone MCP-server reachability probe.

McpOrganizationUsageItem.doc: One account's share of the organization budget, nested in GetMcpOrganizationUsageResponse.

fields.name: userPrincipalName
fields.doc: Absent for rows written before the UPN was recorded.

fields.name: delegated
fields.doc: True when the account is a delegated (MSP) administrator homed in another tenant.

fields.name: homeTenantId
fields.doc: The delegated administrator's home tenant; absent for the tenant's own members.

fields.name: lastRequestAt
fields.doc: Absent for rows written before the timestamp was recorded.

McpQuotaExceededResponse.doc: 429 body written by McpQuotaEnforcementMiddleware when the per-user MCP daily/monthly quota is exhausted (structurally a success shape: first key is quotaExceeded).

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: Which window was exceeded ("daily"/"monthly") — always set on the blocked path.

fields.name: level
fields.doc: Whose budget was exceeded: "user" (the caller's own plan) or "tenant" (the organization-wide windows).

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Limit of the exceeded window.

fields.name: used
fields.doc: Used count of the exceeded window.

fields.name: resetUtc
fields.doc: Reset time of the exceeded window, pre-formatted "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ".

fields.name: targetTenantId
fields.doc: The MANAGED tenant whose organization windows blocked a delegated (MSP) read — its plan governs the budget, not the caller's. Absent when the caller's own tenant/plan was exceeded and on the all-managed-tenants-exhausted aggregate block.

McpUsageQuotaNode.doc: Effective quota state nested in GetMyMcpUsageResponse: the caller's own windows and the organization-wide windows of their tenant (shared by every member; 0 = unlimited). For a delegated (MSP) caller the tenant windows are those of their HOME tenant — reads into managed tenants are charged to the managed tenant per request and never appear here.

MetricsSummaryResponse.doc: Per-tenant session-status tally envelope shared by MetricsSummary and MetricsSummaryGlobal.

MetricsSummaryTenantItem.doc: One per-tenant status tally in MetricsSummaryResponse. WindowDays is repeated per item (envelope carries it too — historical wire shape, kept for parity).

fields.name: failureRate
fields.doc: Failed over the TERMINAL outcomes only (Succeeded + Failed), percent rounded to one decimal; 0 without terminal sessions.

NotificationListResponse.doc: Shared response of GET global/notifications and GET notifications: the active (non-dismissed) notifications visible to the caller, newest first.

NvdRefreshRunWire.doc: Outcome of the last NVD stale-cache refresh walk on THIS instance (in-memory).

fields.name: skippedThrottled
fields.doc: Stale entries left untouched because NVD opened its throttle cooldown mid-run.

fields.name: startedUtc
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 start timestamp.

fields.name: finishedUtc
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 finish timestamp, or null (key omitted) while still running.

OffboardResponse.doc: 202/200 response body for the offboarding endpoint. Fields point the caller at the History row so subsequent reporting / status polling can resolve back to the audit trail. EarliestProcessingAt drives the "data deletion starts in mm ss" countdown in the Web UI's drain-barrier state.

fields.name: earliestProcessingAt
fields.doc: UTC timestamp before which the worker MUST NOT start Phase 2. Drives the cache-drain-barrier countdown UI. Absent on the idempotent-Completed/Failed branches.

OpsEventListResponse.doc: Response of GET global/ops-events, paged and non-paged: the non-paged variant leaves NextLink null so the key is absent, exactly like the old literal.

fields.name: nextLink
fields.doc: Absolute-path link to the next page, or null on the last page / non-paged variant — the key is omitted when null.

PercentileStats.doc: Distribution of a per-session statistic across a version bucket.

fields.name: sampleCount
fields.doc: Number of sessions contributing to the duration distribution (after the >0 filter).

fields.name: clampedSessionCount
fields.doc: Number of sessions whose raw duration exceeded the clamp ceiling and were capped before aggregation. A non-zero value flags stuck/non-terminal sessions skewing the window — the percentiles above are computed on the clamped values, not the runaway wall-clock duration.

PlanTierDefinition.doc: Defines a usage plan tier with request limits: the per-USER windows every account on the plan gets, and the organization-wide TENANT windows all members of a tenant on this plan share. Callers must compare THIS against SessionLimit to decide whether the window was truncated — Sessions.Count understates truncation on fleets where many sessions emit no agent_metrics_snapshot.

Incremented during registration/ingest/login; the daily maintenance recompute treats every cumulative counter as a monotonic "since release" high-water-mark (raise-only — the scanned tables are retention-pruned, so a raw recompute would regress the figures). ReducerVerificationReport.doc: Structural health report for a session's persisted SignalLog + DecisionTransitions journal. Produced by GET /api/sessions/{id}/reducer-verification (Plan §M5, admin/ops endpoint, not tenant-exposed). Scope: this report covers structural invariants that can be checked without running the reducer — ordinal contiguity, cross-references, ReducerVersion drift, counts. A full engine replay with per-step diff would require polymorphic deserialisation of the DecisionSignal.Evidence payload and is a dedicated follow-up.

fields.name: storedReducerVersion
fields.doc: First transition's ReducerVersion (null when no transitions present).

fields.name: currentReducerVersion
fields.doc: The current live backend DecisionEngine.ReducerVersion.

fields.name: reducerVersionDrift
fields.doc: True when stored ≠ current — the session was journaled under a different reducer build. Plan §2.10 calls this out as a known drift signal rather than a bug; the report surfaces it so ops can decide if replay is still meaningful.

fields.name: orphanedTransitionCount
fields.doc: Transitions whose SignalOrdinalRef does not match any loaded signal row. A non-zero count indicates either a corrupted journal or — more likely — truncated data on the query (the verifier loaded a subset of transitions and the referenced signals fell outside the slice).

fields.name: semanticReplayPerformed
fields.doc: True when the verifier re-played the persisted signal stream through the live backend DecisionEngine and compared the produced transitions to the stored journal. False when the replay was skipped — see SemanticReplaySkipReason.

fields.name: semanticReplaySkipReason
fields.doc: Discriminator when SemanticReplayPerformed is false. Known values: "empty_session", "reducer_version_drift", "non_contiguous_signal_ordinals", "non_contiguous_step_indices", "deserialization_failure".

fields.name: semanticReplayFinalStageMatches
fields.doc: True when the replayed Stage matches the ToStage of the last stored transition. Only meaningful when SemanticReplayPerformed is true.

fields.name: replayedFinalStage
fields.doc: The stage the replay arrived at (stringified SessionStage); null on skip.

fields.name: transitionDivergenceCount
fields.doc: Number of positions where the replayed transition diverged from the stored one on the compared fields (Trigger, FromStage, ToStage, Taken, DeadEndReason, StepIndex). 0 means perfect agreement. Individual divergences are emitted as replay_divergenceVerificationIssues up to a cap of 20.

fields.name: issues

ReseedFromGitHubResponse.doc: Response of POST rules/reseed-from-github: per-catalog reseed counters.

ReseedImeLogPatternsResponse.doc: Response of POST rules/ime-log-patterns/reseed (Global Admin only).

fields.doc: Orphan per-tenant RuleState rows cleaned while sunsetting rules missing from the new catalog.

fields.name: sunsetSkipped
